newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-MAHALEL THRUSTS SAUDI ARABIA INTO QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAHALEL THRUSTS SAUDI ARABIA INTO QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Striker Fahad Mahalel lifted his goal tally to three in two games as he propelled Saudi Arabia to a 1-0 win over arch rivals Iraq on Sunday and an Asian Cup quarter-final berth.

Saudi Arabia, beaten finalists in 1992 and winners in 1984 and 1988, were well worth their win and looked capable of going all the way in the 12-nation competition. They now lead group B with two wins out of two games.
Mahalel hit what proved to be the winner after 26 minutes, controlling a pass from Khaled Al Temawi, slipping his marker and firing a 20-metre left-foot shot past goalkeeper Emad Hassan.
That strike added to the two goals Mahalel scored against Thailand in Saudi Arabia's opening match last week.
Midfielder Khalid Al Mowalad should have made it 2-0 four minutes later when, with the Iraqi goal wide open, he shot over the bar from six metres.

Qahtan Drain came close to equalising in the 34th minute when his shot from the edge of the penalty area got a slight deflection and hit the woodwork with Saudi goalkeeper Mohammed al-Daeyea well beaten.
Iraq began the second half strongly and attacked in waves but found al-Daeyea -- one of the Saudi stars in the 1994 World Cup -- in fine form.
He made several crucial interceptions and saves, the best of which was in the 68th minute when he blocked a point- blank shot from Shihaib.
Saudi Arabia suffered a blow in the 58th minute when central defender Mohammed Al Khiliawi had to be taken off on a stretcher with an apparent serious leg injury.
There was no sign of any tension between Saudi Arabia and Iraq supporters as both sides put aside political differences between their two governments.
But with both sets of fans -- 5,000 Saudis and 1,000 Iraqi - - in good voice, there were some political snipes. Saudis waved pictures of King Fahad while Iraqis chanted ''Salute the Iraq''.
Saudi Arabia was the launching pad for a U.S.-led international coalition force that drove Iraq from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.

Iraq: 1-Emad Hassan, 2-Samir Hassan; 3-Walid Afat (8-Mohamed Mehdi 75), 4-Abdul Jabar Hanoon, 5-Radhi Swadi, 6-Esam Salem (19-Ahmed Karim 86), 7-Khalid Sabbar, 10-Qahtan Drain, 12-Hayder Majeed, 15-Husam Naji, 17-Laith Shihaib.

Saudi Arabia: 1-Mohammed al-Daeyea, 2-Mohammed Al Jahani, 3-Mohammed Khilaiwi (24-Khamis Al Zahrani 58), 4-Abdullah Zubromawi, 5-Ahmed Madani, 8-Khaled Al Temawi, 9-Sami Al Jaber (25-Abdullah Al Dossary 46), 10-Fahad Mahalel (12-Ibrahim Al Harbi 75), 13-Hussein Sulimani, 14-Khalid Al Mowalad, 16-Khamis Al Dossary.
